name: Kiwi before bed

lead: This practice is eating kiwifruit shortly before bed in the hope of better sleep, which adherents link to skin, recovery and a more rested look.

Kiwifruit is about 83 percent water and rich in vitamin C and vitamin K, with carotenoids and fibre. The reference source consulted does not describe a sleep mechanism, and published trials of kiwifruit and self-reported sleep are small; no appearance outcomes have been studied.

paras: People eat a kiwi or two in the hour or so before bed as an easy food swap, usually as part of a broader evening routine.
Kiwifruit allergy, first described in 1981, ranges from oral itching to anaphylaxis, and the enzyme actinidain is an allergen for some people.

web.title: Effect of kiwifruit consumption on sleep quality in adults with sleep problems

angle.text: Some people eat kiwifruit before bed as a food-based sleep aid, hoping for better sleep and a more rested look. Small trials have looked at self-reported sleep; appearance outcomes have not been studied.

lead: Eating kiwifruit shortly before bed is a food-based practice that some people adopt to sleep better. Practitioners link better sleep to how they look, through skin, energy and recovery, so a bedtime kiwi is treated as a simple evening routine rather than a supplement.[1]

A 2011 study from Taipei Medical University had 24 adults with self-reported sleep disturbances eat two kiwifruits an hour before bed nightly for four weeks; sleep questionnaire scores, time awake after sleep onset and time to fall asleep fell, and total sleep time and sleep efficiency rose.[1] The authors noted the free-living, self-controlled design and suggested further investigation may be warranted.[1]

Wikipedia describes kiwifruit as about 83% water, rich in vitamin C and vitamin K, with carotenoids and fibre, and notes that kiwifruit allergy ranges from oral symptoms to anaphylaxis. The 2011 paper proposed that serotonin, antioxidants and folate in the fruit could be involved.[1]
infobox: About 83% water; high in vitamin C and K
Kiwifruit allergy ranges from oral symptoms to anaphylaxis

paras: The practice is eating kiwifruit in the evening, before bed. Wikipedia's kiwifruit article covers nutrition and allergy but does not discuss sleep.

The authors of the 2011 study noted that kiwifruit contains antioxidants, vitamins C and E, carotenoids, folate and roughly twice the serotonin of tomatoes, and suggested these could plausibly relate to sleep.[1] Whether any of these compounds explains an effect on sleep was not tested.

Kiwifruit allergy was first described in 1981 and ranges from localised oral allergy syndrome to life-threatening anaphylaxis; wheezing is the most common severe symptom, and the enzyme actinidain can trigger reactions in some people.

The 2011 trial by Lin and colleagues enrolled 24 adults aged 20 to 55 (22 women, 2 men) with self-reported sleep problems. After four weeks of eating two kiwifruits an hour before bed, the Chinese version of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score fell 42.4%, time awake after sleep onset fell 28.9% and sleep onset latency fell 35.4%, while total sleep time rose 13.4% and sleep efficiency rose 5.41%, measured by questionnaire, diary and wrist actigraphy.[1] The study compared participants with themselves before and after and had no separate control group.[1] No studies examined appearance outcomes.

timeline.event: Taipei Medical University researchers publish a four-week study of kiwifruit before bed in adults with sleep problems.[1]
